# 9nth Dimension

> Practical guidance for every stage of spiritual growth, from first questions to a life of quiet peace. Find where you are on the Spiritual Ladder and take the next step.

## The Spiritual Ladder

- [Rung 1: Awakening — when you sense there is more](https://rogenie.github.io/9nthdimension-site/ladder/awakening/): The first stage of spiritual growth is a quiet restlessness. Learn the signs of spiritual awakening, what is happening, and how to take your first real step.
- [Rung 2: Foundations — prayer, gratitude and stillness as daily habits](https://rogenie.github.io/9nthdimension-site/ladder/foundations/): Spiritual growth needs a foundation of small daily habits. Learn how to build a simple prayer, gratitude and stillness routine that actually lasts.
- [Rung 3: Practice — faith in action through intention and discipline](https://rogenie.github.io/9nthdimension-site/ladder/practice/): The third stage of spiritual growth is living your faith, not just studying it. Learn how intention, discipline and consistency turn belief into a changed life.
- [Rung 4: Healing — forgiveness, inner work and discernment](https://rogenie.github.io/9nthdimension-site/ladder/healing/): The fourth stage of spiritual growth is inner healing. Learn how forgiveness, honest inner work and discernment free you from what holds you back.
- [Rung 5: Purpose — finding your gifts, calling and how to serve](https://rogenie.github.io/9nthdimension-site/ladder/purpose/): The fifth stage of spiritual growth is purpose. Learn how to recognise your gifts, discern your calling and turn your growth into service to others.
- [Rung 6: Abiding — living from peace and connection, not effort](https://rogenie.github.io/9nthdimension-site/ladder/abiding/): The sixth stage of spiritual growth is abiding: a steady life lived from peace and connection with God rather than striving. Learn what it looks like and how to stay there.

## Articles

- [What to do when prayer feels dry](https://rogenie.github.io/9nthdimension-site/ladder/healing/what-to-do-when-prayer-feels-dry/): Dry prayer is a normal stage of spiritual growth, not proof that God is gone. Here's why it happens and five practical ways to keep praying through it.
